course_name_original: Diseño y Análisis de Sistemas Térmicos
course_name_en: Design and Analysis of Thermal Systems
prerequisites: Basic knowledge from Engineering degree or equivalent, with training in Physics and Mathematics.
Heat Transfer (convection and conduction without phase change)

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that must be largely self-directed or autonomous.
The ability to solve problems in new or little-known environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
Achieving the ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

The ability for autonomous learning that allows continuing to study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Fundamental analysis of fluid-mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses.
Carrying out elementary calculations for sizing, selection of machines and equipment, and operation for installations with fluids with energy transfers.
Ability to study, propose, and apply different types of technologies to improve the use and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.
Ability for thermodynamic and economic analysis of installations and their elements, for the evaluation of energy efficiency.
Understand current research lines for optimizing energy use in complex heat exchanger systems.
Design the basic equipment and systems of industrial thermal installations.
Identify the variables that influence the operation of thermal equipment and systems.
Apply modeling and dynamic simulation tools to the analysis of the operation of thermal equipment and systems.
Propose and evaluate improved design solutions for thermal equipment and systems taking into account technical, energetic, economic and/or environmental criteria.
Search and analyze specialized documentation in scientific journals and other sources of information.
Synthesize specialized documentation in scientific journals and other sources of information.
Write and present reports of scientific works in the area of the subject.
Write scientific publications as a result of national/international work.

syllabus_topics: Design, modeling and simulation of heat exchange and mass transfer systems in steady and variable regimes.

Application to practical cases of interest in building and industry: heat exchanger networks, drying systems, solar thermal systems, heat accumulators, heat recovery systems, heat pumps, systems with condensation, etc.
Study of a solar thermal installation for DHW using simulation in variable regime
Improvement techniques in heat transfer processes in general and their detailed application to condensation processes.

Wilson method as an experimental technique to obtain correlations for calculating convection coefficients and its detailed application to condensation processes. Different application examples in practical cases.

Simulation of condensation processes of mixtures based on heat and mass transfer equations and its detailed application to the condensation process of the NH3-H2O mixture in absorption refrigeration systems.
Modeling of a DHW installation using solar thermal collectors and its analysis in variable regime over a year of use.
teaching_methods: Individual research of a practical case
assessment_rules: For students with continuous evaluation, if the written exam score (EX) is 4 or higher, the final grade (NOTA) is calculated as (0.2 x IP) + (0.2 x EE) + (0.15 x AC) + (0.45 x EX). If EX is less than 4, NOTA = EX. A minimum course score of 5.0 is required to pass. For students with differentiated evaluation, if EX is 4 or higher, NOTA = (0.2 x EE) + (0.8 x EX); otherwise, NOTA = EX. For extraordinary calls for continuous evaluation students, if a minimum of 4 points in the theoretical exam (EX) is achieved, NOTA = (0.2 x IP) + (0.2 x EE) + (0.15 x AC) + (0.45 x EX), using prior IP, EE, and AC scores; otherwise, NOTA = EX. For differentiated evaluation students in extraordinary calls, NOTA is the score obtained in the theoretical exam.
